content:
New Jersey prospects kick off their two-game Rookie Showcase against the Islanders as the home team at RWJBarnabas Health Hockey House on Sunday afternoon. Puck drop is 2 p.m. ET. Anton Silaev makes his Rookie Showcase debut on Sunday. It didn’t take long for the Devils rookies to shift from practice mode to game mode. After just one day of practice, the Devils will welcome the Islanders to RWJBarnabas Health Hockey House on Sunday for the first of two Rookie Camp showcase games between the clubs. Puck drop is set for 2 p.m., with the game available to stream live on livestreamed on the Devils' official website. For the rookies, it’s an opportunity to take everything they’ve worked on over the first day of camp and put it into game action and make a quick impression. With a mix of returning prospects, recent draft picks and players looking to make an impression, Sunday’s matchup will offer the first chance to see how the group comes together when the competition ramps up. The Devils have just a single first-round pick on its roster with Anton Silaev making his debut. He was drafted 10th overall in 2024. The roster also has two second-round picks, both with NHL experience, Seamus Casey and Lenni Hämeenaho. The roster includes four fourth-round picks, three sixth rounders, one seventh and three free agent invites. For the Islanders, they boast three first-round picks, including two of their 2025 first rounders in Victor Eklund (16th overall) and Kashawn Aitcheson (17th overall). The Islanders have two second-round picks, two third and fourth round picks, a fifth and seventh round pick as well as several undrafted players as the makeup of their 25-man roster. The showcase game is one of two games the rookies will play this Rookie Camp, both against the Islanders. The Devils will visit the Isles on Tuesday. Sunday marks the Rookie Camp debut of 2024 first-round pick defenseman Anton Silaev. The 20-year-old stands at 6-foot-7 and towers over his teammates, but perhaps what stands out most is how smoothly he moves for a player of his size. Silaev's skating is a major part of his game. He covers a lot of ice and has the mobility to close gaps quickly. He has a long reach that can make life difficult for opposing forwards, and his size gives him plenty of upside as he starts to adjust to the North American game. Silaev was paired with Seamus Casey during the club's practice on Saturday, and the two are expected to be paired together against the Islanders. It'll be an interesting first look at Silaev in a game setting and, for Devils fans, a chance to see what that combination of size, skating and puck-moving ability looks like against competition. Eiserman is a 20-year-old forward with aspirations of making a push for a roster spot on the Islanders. He was selected 10 spots after Silaev, 20th overall in 2024, by New York. He has a bit of AHL experience after finishing out his Boston University career, playing 12 games with Bridgeport last season. Eiserman owns a pretty wicked NHL-caliber shot and has always been known for his ability to score goals, putting up 72 goals in 58 games during his final season with the USNTDP. He'll be looking to turn that scoring touch into an NHL opportunity this season, and with another year of development under his belt, he'll be one of the younger players in the Islanders' mix pushing for a spot. title: He Bought a Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing, Drove 3,800 Miles, Is Selling It Because He Hates the Color - autoevolution
content:
The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing is finished in Deep Space Metallic, an option costing $625, over a Sky Cool Gray and Jet Black interior and rides on 19-inch wheels in Satin Graphite Dark Finish. So what is not to like about it? However, the owner hates it. "I am more of an orange, yellow, Kawasaki Green guy," he explains. Why didn't he buy a Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing in one of those colors in the first place? He says he practically begged Cadillac to sell him a car painted a color that was not on their list, but his request was met with multiple NOs. However, he wanted a Blackwing because it was the final high-performance car with a stick shift before Cadillac pulled the plug on it. Several months after the car was delivered to him, the automaker came up with the Curated program, which offered 160 colors to choose from. Well, wealthy or not, a brand-new Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing starts at $100,695 before checking the box for the optional Precision Package that this car comes with or the custom orange paint that his next car will wear. The Precision Package is a $18,000 option on the Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing. It doesn't add extra oomph, but it completely overhauls the car's suspension, alignment capability, and braking performance to cut down lap times. The owner says he road-tripped the Caddy to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas, for the WEC race last year, adding approximately 2,000 miles. For the rest, he just poked around town or went to car meets on Thursdays. That is what makes it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.6 seconds when equipped with the six-speed manual transmission like this car is. The one with the auto box is 0.2 seconds quicker. It takes 11.7 seconds down the quarter mile and hits a top speed of 200 mph (322 kph). An electronic limited-slip differential and the Magnetic Ride Control are part of the plan to make the performance sedan easier to maneuver and more comfortable to ride in. An Ultra View sunroof shelters the cabin, which hosts heated and ventilated front seats. An HD Surround Vision camera provides the soundtrack when the driver has had enough of the V8 supercharged orchestra. Even if it is still a new car, it still comes with some flaws, and the most annoying one is the fact that the seat massagers on the bolsters and lumbar adjustment functions on the front seats are inoperative. He explains that he just didn’t want to argue with Cadillac or explain why there is interior damage on the car that he was planning to sell anyway. So, this is something that the buyer will have to solve. The list of flaws also includes indentation above the front grille, some missing windshield gasket top pieces that he has no idea how he lost, and the fact that the gauges occasionally reset from Track to Tour mode. The car came from the factory wearing the Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2R tires, but the owner swapped them for Pilot Sport 4S units at 222 miles (357 kilometers). The previous ones were terrible in the rain, he complains. The engine oil and filter were changed earlier this month at 3,786 miles. The front view camera, steering column lock module, nd ttelamtics control module were reprogrammed in June 2026. All four tires were replaced in August 2025. The window sticker indicates that the original owner, the man selling it now, paid $125,110 to drive it off the showroom floor. Now, with six days to go to the end of the auction, the highest bid sits at $86,000 and counting. The one who places the winning bid will also get two keys, service records, lug nuts and a key, two foam brake rotor protectors, a tire inflator, and the tow eyebolt, along with a clean Carfax report showing no accidents or mileage discrepancies. Elena started off as a sports reporter and five years later switched to automotive. How does that happen? Lots of writing, testdrives, traveling, off-road driving courses, track driving courses, defensive driving courses and diplomas. The diplomas might be "useless", but the knowledge she gained is priceless.

title: Diablo V: Forging the Next Era - Blizzard News
content:
Igniting our celebration of 30 years, we unveiled the Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel at BlizzCon 2026. The development team revealed the first details of the world, classes, and systems taking shape in Diablo V. You’ll become the Heir to Westmarch and traverse a Sanctuary actively reshaped by Diablo, accompanied by a growing caravan of survivors. The team also unveiled the Demon Hunter, Monk, and all-new Plague Knight classes and shared how past Diablo games are inspiring a renewed focus on item depth, clarity, and identity. These early ideas all flow from the central premise at the heart of Diablo V: the heroes of the past have failed, Sanctuary has fallen, and Diablo has won. This is the foundation for Diablo’s next era, and only the beginning of what the team plans to share as development continues. Catch up on the full Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel here: Diablo has conquered Sanctuary, a stepping stone to invading the Heavens. Now from the throne of Westmarch, he wields Sanctuary's people and souls as weapons in the Eternal Conflict. Diablo is no longer a distant threat waiting at the end of the journey. He is present from the moment Diablo V begins, shaping the story, the world, and your path through it. As Heir to Westmarch, on the run through the charred remains of a kingdom now transformed into an outpost of Hell. Few humans have escaped Diablo’s rule. Some have bowed before him or joined his cults, while a terrifying few have been corrupted into Dread Commanders and raised to rival the powers of Hell. Your mysterious connection to Diablo makes you both a threat and uniquely vulnerable to his powerful influence. With Sanctuary’s greatest champions gone, what must you become to fight for the home taken from you? This is not Sanctuary waiting for the apocalypse. It is already living through one. In Diablo V, humanity has fallen into ruin, and the Western Continent is at the heart of Diablo’s reign of terror. We revealed a haunting, desolate land shaped by despair, resilience, and the few survivors fighting to endure another day. Sanctuary itself is no longer stable. Diablo is actively reshaping the world through terror, reflected by a procedural landscape where terrain, points of interest, monsters, and reward can change when you return. It’s ruins tell the story of what was lost, its corruption reveals Diablo’s present rule, and the encroaching forces of Hell offer a glimpse of what comes next. With Sanctuary under Diablo’s rule, survival is no longer tied to towns or conquered strongholds. Instead, you’ll need to build a caravan of allies who travel with you through the scorched wastes. These allies will be both vendors and steadfast companions, a growing community full of stories to discover. They are fascinating characters with pasts, stakes, and scars from surviving in Diablo’s Sanctuary. Amongst your newfound companions are a former Sister of the Sightless Eye... and a stranded Treasure Goblin searching for meaning in a world where greed has lost its purpose. The team offered an early look at how they’re thinking about class identity, progression, and loot. During the panel, we revealed the first three classes coming to Diablo V: The Demon Hunter returns to stalk the forces of Hell with twin crossbows, striking from the shadows and leaping across the battlefield to annihilate their prey. The Monk brings martial perfection back to Sanctuary, battering demons to a pulp with fists and calling down holy power to smite those who stand in their path. The all-new Plague Knight is the embodiment of walking death. They roam the battlefield, spreading disease and pestilence, ultimately consuming it for power. These are only the first of the classes we’ll reveal on the road to Diablo V, with more details on their combat, progression, and build possibilities to come. The team emphasized their goal is to design items to feel readable, memorable, and worth chasing across hundreds of hours. Itemization in Diablo V is inspired by Diablo II. We’re experimenting with stat requirements on gear. Your inventory plays a key role in how you wield your arsenal, larger items once again take up more slots in your inventory. Gear-based sets are also returning for Diablo V. This will be a rich and deep crafting system, inspired by Lord of Hatred’s approach, with Diablo II-style Runes and Runewords. Diablo V is still early in development, and this reveal marks the beginning of an ongoing conversation with the Diablo player community. Starting in 2027, we plan to share regular updates offering a closer look at our progress, the ideas guiding development, and features taking shape along the way. Bringing players into the process early gives us the opportunity to listen, understand what excites you the most, and allow that to inform the decisions ahead. We want to build a Diablo game that honors what players love while taking the series somewhere genuinely new. The next era has only begun. Sign up for future updates at Diablo5.Blizzard.com. title: Diablo V First Look: Blizzard’s Next Sequel Doubles Down on Darkness - Esquire
content: Only three years after Diablo IV, Blizzard reveals the next sequel of its hit RPG series exclusively to Esquire. The end is now. Three and a half years after Diablo IV, Blizzard Entertainment is announcing the next installment in its popular action role-playing series: Diablo V. For the first time in more than 15 years, players will square off with the Big D himself, Diablo, who has changed quite a bit since he rose as the ultimate Prime Evil. Diablo V is scheduled to launch in 2029 on platforms Blizzard has yet to announce. “You’re entering Diablo V with Sanctuary in an apocalypse,” says Joe Shely, senior game director, in an exclusive interview with Esquire. “Sanctuary is not a happy place in the best of times, but Diablo V takes it to another level. You’re living in a world that has been overrun by Diablo. He sits on the throne, humanity is destroyed, and players themselves are on the run.” “You’ve spent the last 30 years fending off the apocalypse,” adds Jennifer Helper, narrative director of Diablo V. “We were like, What if Diablo won and we scramble to claw back territory by our fingernails? We wanted to make a world that’s darker than ever but give you a reason to fight for it.” Ahead of the game’s reveal at BlizzCon in Anaheim, California, Esquire sat down with members of the game’s senior development team, who peeled back the curtain on players’ next adventure across Sanctuary as it has fallen under Diablo’s occupation. Next to Shely and Helper is John Mueller, Diablo V’s senior art director. Together they tell Esquire that the driving question behind the new project was “Wouldn’t it be cool if…?” Wouldn’t it be cool if … we brought back fan-favorite classes? Wouldn’t it be cool if … there was a single memorable space full of interesting people? Wouldn’t it be cool if … the story was centered entirely on the players’ characters? These questions drove Blizzard to pursue a full-fledged entry in the mainline series. Usually a new game coming a few years after the previous installment isn’t so earth-shattering for a hit video game series. But Diablo is not an ordinary series. Since Diablo II was released in 2000, fans have spent literal decades waiting for just a glimpse of sequels like Diablo III (released in 2012) and Diablo IV (released in 2023). Waiting out epochs is routine for fans. But all their waiting and wondering for what’s next ends now. What’s next is a heated reunion with Diablo. Esquire has the first-ever exclusive look at Diablo V with its concept art below. “We wanted to turn back to the title villain, who we haven’t seen in over ten years, since Diablo III,” says Shely. “He needs his own game. There are things we can do, in terms of innovations and how we tell the story, that give us a fresh slate.” Set a century after Diablo IV, Diablo V casts players as the runaway heir to the lost kingdom of Westmarch. They share a mysterious connection with Diablo, who has since evolved from a big, bad guy of fire and brimstone into a more calculated antagonist. “We wanted to give players a lot of agency in the story,” explains Helper, the main architect of Diablo V’s story. In contrast to how players spend time in Diablo IV forging connections with Lilith and Mephisto, Helper says they wanted players to feel their bonds “much faster” in Diablo V. “The story starts when you find you’re the only one who can go into Diablo’s terror realm and come back alive,” she says. “We wanted to give you that core identity we could build the story around. You’re not a wanderer in someone else’s story.” Helper adds: “In past games, Diablo was brutish. What did Diablo learn from watching Mephisto? Diablo has learned how to be subtle. He is the Lord of Terror; what does terror mean? What does someone whose entire existence is provoking or feeding on fear going to be like? We want to give you that bond with him from the beginning. Why is Diablo interested in you? How you define yourself in the shadow of, and in opposition to, Diablo is a big part of the game. He is trying to control you. What do you do to push back?” Helper clarifies that players still retain plenty of individual customization over their characters, like in their character classes. “You aren’t a fixed character. This is not Nathan Drake. This is still an ARPG. The Heir to Westmarch in your world is whatever gender and class you pick.” “You’ll shape who you are as a character, as the heir, more freely than you ever have before,” adds Joe Shely. “The idea of who you are as a person and what class you’re playing are independent in a way they’ve never been before. You can look and be whoever you want.” Speaking of classes, Shely says Diablo V “will launch with more classes than we ever had in a Diablo game before.” While the team cannot unpack each class in detail yet, it is revealing three in particular: the returning Monk and Demon Hunter, as well as the new Plague Knight. “The Monk and Demon Hunter are really established fantasies for us,” says John Mueller, who oversees the art direction of Diablo V. “The last time players saw these was Diablo III. In 2012, technology was different. We have advanced through Diablo IV, so we want to give people the best versions of these in 2029.” Shely lays out the Demon Hunter’s and Monk’s individual vibes, in case you weren’t around for Diablo III. “A Demon Hunter has light armor and twin crossbows. They’re extremely agile, pinning demons against walls. It’s a fantasy players are familiar with. And Monk, you know, who doesn’t like pulverizing demons with their fist? It’s an up-close melee class.” Then there’s the Plague Knight, a new control-based character built like a tank that spreads disease. “This is a heavily armored, ‘walking death’ character who will spread disease across the battlefield and consume that disease for power.” Artistically, the team designed the Plague Knight like a medieval iron maiden on two legs. As in any action RPG, players start the game with almost nothing. Over time, they meet new allies who join their nomadic caravan as it roves through a desolate Sanctuary. Blizzard says the caravan serves as the players’ main hub—the only “safe space” in a hellish world—and that it will physically evolve as players progress through the story. “We need there to be something you love about this world,” says Helper. “Gathering survivors is one of the mechanisms of the story. We’re going through lands where almost everybody is dead or surrendered to Diablo. Now and then we meet a person who has held out, and they become part of the caravan. Your vendors, your craftspeople, everyone who is part of your journey are survivors. These are the people you’re fighting to protect and the source of all your side content.” Helper reveals that the caravan will change over time as players find new survivors and level up. “Each wagon reflects their personality and background. The wagons upgrade as you go on, reflecting things you’ve done in the story. Trophies from victories appear at the campsite. It becomes a really dynamic place that tracks you in the game.” Adds Mueller, “You start this ragtag [operation]. It’s a shoddy situation. By the end, you’ve grown that into a very aspirational space you love going back to. We think that’s going to be a fun, dynamic way to experience the story.” If Diablo sounds darker than it’s ever been before, which says a lot for a series that’s long epitomized grim-dark video games, that’s by design. Blizzard intends Diablo V to feel bleak and hopeless, which can make every win shine brighter. “We’re doubling down on the darkness,” says Mueller. “Evil has infected everything. Civilization is devastated. The architecture is devastated. Even time has ravaged what’s been left behind. You have this apocalyptic vision of Sanctuary, and for a medieval dark fantasy, it is really compelling.” To that end, Diablo V is returning the franchise to a procedural dungeon system that’s been leveled up with modern software. There is a hundred years’ worth of horror that happened, which players will learn from the environment. “People will want to know what happened in the last hundred years as you’re exploring,” reveals Mueller. “The world is procedural; this is our third generation of procedural dungeon tech. People will get everything they got from the open world of Diablo IV in a dynamic way. You see stories of the past. Stories of survival and tragedy. This is where art is collaborating with narrative closer than ever.” Shely says that the world generation occurs as players move their caravan through the fog of war, like a rickety wagon in a frontier western epic. “The caravan itself moves through the world. It’s not a town that exists in a space. You’re taking your ‘town’ with you through this dangerous place that’s been transformed by the Dread Commanders. You explore, go through the world, and then return to that area with your caravan, and it’s been totally transformed.” While players might think work on Diablo V has just begun, it’s actually been in development for years. There is still more to learn about the game. It won’t release until 2029, which affords anyone still playing through Diablo IV more time to enjoy new, forthcoming content (like Season of Hell’s Legacy, which launches on September 15 to mark the series’ 30th anniversary). When Diablo V eventually arrives, it’ll be about two years into the next console generation. When Esquire asks how Blizzard is developing Diablo V on upcoming platforms, the team keeps mum. “Generally speaking, Blizzard wants to bring our games to as many players as possible,” says Shely, “and so we seek to make Diablo available on many platforms. You can see that with Diablo IV. You should expect the same with Diablo V. We want everyone to take on the Lord of Terror.” For now, all fans should know is that Diablo V is real, and it’s happening sooner than they might have assumed. And waiting for all of them on the long road ahead is one more fight with Diablo. title: BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: Starcraft Returns, Diablo V Announced, Warcraft news and more - XBOX Wire
content: I’ve been at Blizzard a long time, and I’ve got a bunch of BlizzCons under my belt. Do you know how hard all these announcements were to hold in as we prepared for BlizzCon 2026? I can’t even believe this is real, man, like…okay, sorry, I’m locked in. Whether you’re watching it all unfold live or just catching up later, here is everything from the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony and where to go next for each one. From the farthest reaches of the stars, a new mission calls. StarCraft returns in 2030 as an original open-world shooter. There is really only one thing to say to that, and we said it from the stage and the halls in Anaheim, California: it’s about damn time. Diablo V is coming in Spring 2029, and it opens somewhere the series has never let us stand: after the loss. Sanctuary has fallen. Diablo has won. The question the game asks is what we become when the world we knew is gone. Closer to now, Diablo IV‘s Season of Hell’s Legacy lands September 15 (that’s this Tuesday!) to mark 30 years of Diablo. It brings back the Prime Evils, the Lord of Terror included, along with Deckard Cain, Nightmare Rifts, anniversary rewards, and gear pulled from every era of the series. A little further out, the Amazon joins as the next Diablo IV class in the first half of 2027, javelin in hand. And if you are at the show or playing from home, Moophisto has returned to terrorize the unsuspecting. He is as udderly malevolent as you remember. Heh. XBOX players can save 75% off Diablo IV and up to 30% on Diablo II: Resurrected content now through September 22nd. Everything coming to Sanctuary is on the Diablo website. Ten years of Overwatch, and the team spent its anniversary talking about what comes next. Season 5’s new Support Hero is Doctrine, a life-draining, vampire-inspired healer who sends out bat-like drones. You can play him at BlizzCon right now, and from home for a limited time. He arrives alongside major reworks for Sombra and Roadhog, plus a new map, Watchpoint: Grimsvotn. Season 5 also closes out The Reign of Talon, the first year-long story arc in Overwatch history, and it does not end quietly. The next Overwatch Spotlight follows in February 2027 with the team’s plans for the year. Two things worth clearing your weekend for: YOASOBI plays BlizzCon’s first-ever halftime show during the Overwatch World Cup, and LE SSERAFIM returns to the Main Stage as the closing act, with a new in-game collaboration live now. Then there is QuestWatch, a live Overwatch tabletop RPG one-shot written by Matt Mercer and the Overwatch Narrative team. For those playing on XBOX while you’re streaming at home: play one match to earn a Mythic Voucher and choose an eligible Mythic Hero Skin! More detail on all of it lives on the Overwatch website. Warcraft Goes Backward and Forward at the Same Time We are at the midpoint of The Worldsoul Saga. World of Warcraft‘s next major update, Eclipse (12.2), has Xal’atath closing in on Azeroth’s Worldsoul, and where that goes is up to us. We also got a look at The Last Titan, the final chapter of the Saga, which brings more than two decades of Warcraft storytelling to a close and sets up whatever comes after. More on that early next year. Then a genuine surprise: for the first time in over 23 years, there is a new Warcraft III: Reforged story. The Forsaken Kingdom campaign takes you back to the fall of Lordaeron and its turn into the Undercity, and it ships with the 3.0 update, which brings a substantial graphics overhaul and a revamped World Editor. It is playable today. We dropped it like a Beyonce album. Warcraft III: Reforged is available with XBOX Game Pass, so you only need to pick up the DLC to jump into the new campaign And then we went home. World of Warcraft: Forever is a third way to play alongside Modern and Classic, set in the Vanilla era, with room to explore corners of Azeroth we never got to see the first time: three new zones, over 1,000 new quests, nine new dungeons, two new raids, and the new Skyborne race. It launches November 4, 2026, with Beta starting September 17. The full Warcraft rundown is on the Warcraft website. Hearthstone Opens a Journal and Meets the Old Gods The overhauled Journal pulls every quest, achievement, and event into one place, tied together by the story of each expansion. It keeps a record of where you have been and grows as you keep playing. Reign of the Black Empire hits the Tavern October 20 and takes Hearthstone to the earliest age of Azeroth, long before the Old Gods were imprisoned. Its new keyword, Assemble, merges two cards into a stronger one, which is going to produce some combinations nobody planned for. Before that, on September 22, Battlegrounds adds a new minion type called Aberrations, grown out of Old God corruption and experimentation. Looking further out, the Monk arrives in March 2027 as the game’s first new playable class in six years, fluid and adaptable in the way the class has always been. Xal’atath joins Heroes of the Storm on September 28, playable on the PTR starting September 14. This one belongs to those of you who never stopped playing. There may even be another hero ahead? What year is this? An animated series set in the world of Diablo is in development with Netflix. More on that later, and it is not the only thing taking shape. The BlizzCon livestream runs all weekend with deep dives, panels, and a halftime show, and the full schedule is on the BlizzCon site so you can plan what you want to watch. If you only take three dates with you: Diablo IV‘s Season of Hell’s Legacy launches on September 15, World of Warcraft: Forever Beta opens September 17, and Forever itself launches November 4.  Dude, we’re so back.

title: Diablo V Is Coming Out In Spring 2029 - Engadget
content: Blizzard also confirmed that a Diablo animated series is in development with Netflix. BlizzCon has brought some unexpected news for the Diablo franchise, including a spring 2029 release window for the next installment in the video game series, as well as a confirmation of an animated TV series adaptation in the works with Netflix. For the game, Blizzard's teaser video and article only hints at the story's continuation after the events of Diablo IV, but it looks like players will be thrown straight into hellfire. Like the Diablo V teaser, the confirmation for the animated TV show was equally light on details and we still don't know the release date or which animation studio is in charge of the adaptation. Blizzard said it will have more to share about the series throughout the development process and only hinted that "Sanctuary's darkness is spreading." For those who aren't devoted Diablo fans, rumors of a TV adaptation for the franchise have been circulating for a while. A report from 2020 hinted that a Diablo TV series would be done in an anime style and was in preproduction with Netflix in charge of distribution. Beyond the confirmation of the fifth major game in the franchise and a TV series, Blizzard also hinted at similar adaptations for its other popular titles, including Overwatch and Warcraft.

content: Get unlimited access to everything VICE has to offer. BlizzCon 2026 included a surprise reveal trailer and release window for Diablo V. BlizzCon 2026’s opening ceremony included a ton of exciting surprise announcements, including the shocking reveal of Diablo V. “The heroes are gone. Sanctuary has hallen. title: Diablo’s Next Era Revealed at BlizzCon 2026: Opening Ceremonies Recap - Blizzard News
content:
Thirty years in, Diablo has never had more content ahead of it than now. During the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, we offered the first glimpse of Diablo V (coming Spring 2029), announced a new animated series set in the world of Diablo in development with Netflix, revealed the Amazon class pack coming to Diablo IV in 2027, unveiled Season of Hell’s Legacy, and confirmed that Diablo IV is coming to Nintendo Switch™ 2. And we’re just getting started. The celebration continues throughout BlizzCon with developer panels, live gameplay, and more from across the franchise, including Diablo Immortal x Spawn. To rewatch BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremonies, you can watch our panel here: Celebrate 30 Years with the Season of Hell’s Legacy Diablo V is officially in development and coming Spring 2029. For the first time, players will enter a Sanctuary where Diablo has triumphed and its heroes have been defeated. At the heart of Diablo V lies a defining question: what must you become when the world has already fallen? Join us for Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel on September 12, 1:45 p.m. PT for an early look at the world, classes and creative vision shaping the chapter of Diablo. You can also sign up for future updates at Diablo5.Blizzard.com. Sanctuary’s darkness is spreading. Blizzard and Netflix are developing a new animated series set in the world of Diablo, bringing the franchise to a new screen. We’ll have more to share as the series takes shape. Until then, stay awhile... and stay tuned. The Amazon is coming to Diablo IV in the first half of 2027. She hails from the island of Skovos, revealed for the first time in Diablo IV in Lord of Hatred. Her return preserves the disciplined, athletic, and highly trained warrior fantasy players remember while reimagining the class for Diablo IV. Across four gameplay archetypes—Champion, Skirmisher, Ranger, and Commander—the Amazon can wield the returning bow and javelin, which introduces an entirely new weapon type to Diablo IV. Get a closer look at the Amazon in the Diablo IV: What's Next panel on September 13, 11:00 a.m. PT. Additional class pack details will be shared at a later date. More than 130 million players worldwide have entered Sanctuary across the Diablo franchise. Now, three decades of darkness return in Season of Hell’s Legacy, a playable tribute to Diablo’s most iconic characters, foes, locations and loot. In Season of Hell's Legacy, the lost soul of Deckard Cain returns to guide you through an epic journey to redeem the dark wanderers from the torment of the Prime Evils. Confront the Prime Evils Baal, Mephisto, and Diablo, reclaim splinters of their souls, and bear the burden of one of the Splinters to assume a portion of their power. But remember: no demonic gift is bestowed without a steep price. Read more of the legacy the Burning Hells has wrought in our Season Overview blog here, and join us for the Diablo IV: What's Next panel on September 13, 11:00 a.m. PT. Hell has arrived on Nintendo Switch™ 2. The Diablo IV: Age of Hatred Collection is coming to Nintendo Switch™ 2 on September 15. The Diablo IV: Age of Hatred Collection bundles the base game, Vessel of Hatred expansion, and Lord of Hatred expansion. Plunder through the jungles of Nahantu and the far-reaching shores of Skovos, Joy-Con 2 Controller in hand, to challenge the Lord of Hatred’s hold over Sanctuary. The 30th anniversary celebration continues throughout BlizzCon weekend with panel highlighting the voice talent behind some of Diablo’s iconic characters and the making of Diablo IV’s cinematics. Join us live at the Anaheim Convention Center or watch from home on the following channels (exceptions noted below): The future of Diablo begins here! Host Johanna Faries sits down with the Diablo V development team to share an early preview of the game's story, world-building approach, class design philosophy, and the vision that will define the next era for Diablo. Join the Diablo IV Cinematic team for a behind-the-scenes look at the visual storytelling, performance, animation, and craft behind Sanctuary's darkest moments. Legendary comic creator Todd McFarlane takes the stage with Diablo Immortal Senior Artist Justin Murray for a live drawing session celebrating the worlds of Spawn and Sanctuary. Watch as the two artists create original artwork in real time, discuss the creative process behind the collaboration, and share insights into bringing one of comics' most iconic antiheroes to Diablo Immortal. Celebrate 30 years of darkness with the Diablo development team for the world premiere of the Season of Hell's Legacy gameplay trailer and a deep dive into the upcoming season that is inspired by iconic moments from across Diablos history. The team will also share an early look at the next class coming to Diablo: the Amazon.
